steps.tx: Autonomous, unregulated hypersecretion of parathyroid hormone represents the single most common cause of hypercalcaemia in the outpatient setting. Encountering **primary hyperparathyroidism** occurs predominantly in postmenopausal women with a female-to-male ratio of three to one. A single benign solitary parathyroid adenoma accounts for eighty-five percent of cases, four-gland parathyroid hyperplasia accounts for fifteen percent, and parathyroid carcinoma accounts for under one percent. Most patients in contemporary practice are asymptomatic, detected on routine biochemical screening showing elevated serum calcium with an inappropriately elevated parathyroid hormone.
steps.say: Autonomous, unregulated hypersecretion of parathyroid hormone represents the most common cause of hypercalcaemia in outpatients. A single solitary adenoma accounts for eighty-five percent of cases, four-gland hyperplasia accounts for fifteen percent, and carcinoma for under one percent. Familial forms occur in multiple endocrine neoplasia syndromes. Most modern patients are asymptomatic, detected on routine biochemical screening.

steps.tx: The eighty-four-amino-acid peptide hormone synthesized by parathyroid chief cells tightly orchestrates systemic calcium and phosphate homeostasis. Circulating **pth** acts directly on osteoblasts and renal tubular epithelial cells, and indirectly on enterocytes. In the distal tubule, it stimulates calcium reabsorption, while in the proximal tubule it promotes phosphaturia. In addition, PTH upregulates renal one-alpha-hydroxylase, synthesizing calcitriol to augment enterocyte calcium absorption. In bone, continuous high PTH levels activate osteoclasts to drive bone resorption and calcium efflux into the circulation.
steps.say: The eighty-four-amino-acid peptide hormone synthesized by parathyroid chief cells tightly orchestrates systemic calcium and phosphate homeostasis. Circulating pth acts directly on osteoblasts and renal tubular epithelial cells, and indirectly on intestinal enterocytes. In the distal tubule, it stimulates calcium reabsorption, while in the proximal tubule it promotes phosphaturia. In addition, PTH upregulates renal one-alpha-hydroxylase to synthesize calcitriol. In bone, continuous PTH stimulates osteoclasts to mobilize skeletal calcium.

steps.tx: Classic multiorgan clinical manifestations of prolonged calcium elevation are historically summarized as stones, bones, abdominal groans, and psychic moans. Developing chronic **hypercalcaemia** promotes nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis from hypercalciuria, causing recurrent calcium oxalate stones. Skeletal involvement manifests as osteopenia and osteitis fibrosa cystica with subperiosteal bone resorption on the radial aspect of the middle phalanges. Gastrointestinal manifestations include constipation, peptic ulcer disease from gastrin stimulation, and acute pancreatitis. Neuropsychiatric manifestations range from fatigue to depression and cognitive slowing.

steps.tx: Distinguishing primary hyperparathyroidism from other hypercalcaemic conditions requires systematic evaluation of parathyroid hormone and urinary calcium excretion. Demonstrating elevated serum calcium paired with an inappropriately elevated intact parathyroid hormone establishes primary hyperparathyroidism. In contrast, **hypercalcaemia of malignancy**, driven by PTHrP from solid tumours or osteolytic bone metastases, suppresses endogenous intact PTH to undetectable levels. Measuring twenty-four-hour urinary calcium excretion is essential to exclude familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia, where an inactivating calcium-sensing receptor mutation produces low urinary calcium excretion.
steps.say: Distinguishing primary hyperparathyroidism from other hypercalcaemic conditions requires evaluating parathyroid hormone and urinary calcium excretion. Demonstrating elevated serum calcium paired with an inappropriately high or non-suppressed parathyroid hormone establishes primary hyperparathyroidism. In contrast, hypercalcaemia of malignancy suppresses intact parathyroid hormone to undetectable levels. Measuring urinary calcium excretion excludes familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia, which features low urinary calcium excretion.

steps.tx: Potent antiresorptive medications providing rapid inhibition of osteoclastic bone destruction constitute the primary medical therapy for acute severe hypercalcaemia. Intravenous **bisphosphonates**, such as zoledronic acid four milligrams or pamidronate sixty to ninety milligrams infused over several hours, bind mineralized hydroxyapatite and inhibit osteoclast farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase. This blockade arrests bone resorption, decreasing serum calcium concentrations within two to four days and reaching nadir at four to seven days. Bisphosphonates are vital for emergency stabilization of symptomatic hypercalcaemic crisis and provide temporary skeletal protection in inoperable primary hyperparathyroidism.

steps.tx: A critical pharmacological strategy manages acute hypercalcaemic emergencies through sequential and coordinated interventions. When corrected serum calcium exceeds fourteen milligrams per decilitre, immediate **fluid resuscitation** with intravenous isotonic saline restores intravascular volume, inducing kaliuresis and calciuresis. Once volume is replete, loop diuretics such as furosemide may be administered cautiously to promote further calcium wasting, while calcitonin provides immediate but transient calcium reduction via tachyphylaxis. Bisphosphonates are concurrently administered to ensure sustained calcium normalization beyond seventy-two hours, with haemodialysis reserved for refractory crisis or end-stage renal disease.

steps.tx: Targeted small-molecule allosteric activators of the extracellular calcium-sensing receptor provide medical control when surgery is contraindicated. Administering oral **cinacalcet** increases the sensitivity of calcium-sensing receptors on parathyroid chief cells to extracellular calcium, suppressing PTH synthesis and secretion without altering parathyroid gland mass. Cinacalcet successfully normalizes serum calcium in up to eighty percent of patients with primary hyperparathyroidism, serving as an effective non-surgical maintenance option for elderly patients with significant comorbidities, inoperable parathyroid carcinoma, or recurrent hyperparathyroidism following subtotal parathyroidectomy.

steps.tx: Definitive curative management of primary hyperparathyroidism is achieved exclusively through surgical resection of the hyperfunctioning parathyroid tissue. Undergoing **parathyroidectomy** is indicated for all symptomatic individuals and for asymptomatic patients meeting international criteria: age under fifty, serum calcium exceeding one milligram per decilitre above normal, or T-score below minus two point five. Preoperative localization using sestamibi SPECT scanning and neck ultrasound enables minimally invasive targeted parathyroidectomy, confirmed intraoperatively by a greater than fifty percent drop in intact parathyroid hormone.
steps.say: Definitive curative management of primary hyperparathyroidism is achieved exclusively through surgical resection of hyperfunctioning parathyroid tissue. Undergoing parathyroidectomy is indicated for all symptomatic patients and asymptomatic patients meeting criteria such as age under fifty, osteoporosis, or renal compromise. Preoperative localization using sestamibi scanning and ultrasound enables minimally invasive surgery, confirmed intraoperatively by a fifty percent drop in parathyroid hormone following adenoma excision.
